texts.text: SPECIAL KEYS

R  Become the Remote Control.
    SPACEBAR toggles on/off.
To continue, press RETURN.

S  Become the Solderpen.
    SPACEBAR solders/unsolders.

This is the REMOTE CONTROL.
It `freezes" the flow of 
electricity.

Press SPACEBAR again to let
electricity flow. The Remote
Control turns orange.

To disconnect the wire, move near
the INPUT or OUTPUT. Press the
SPACEBAR when the tip glows
orange.

`Freeze" the
electricity to
stop the robot.

Turn on the elec-
tricity and the
robot moves.





When the Remote
Control is on, it
drains electricity
from the robot's
battery.

Freeze the electricity again.

Pick up the sensor and move it
around the crystal.

Do the outputs
change color?

Sensors don't work when the
Remote Control is off.

Turn the Remote Control on.

The SOLDERPEN is used
to wire OUTPUTS to
INPUTS.

Press S to become the
Solderpen.

Move the Solderpen to the
INPUT (circle) until the
Solderpen tip glows
orange. Press SPACEBAR.

Move the Solderpen to the
OUTPUT (arrow). When the
tip glows orange, press
SPACEBAR. The INPUT is
now wired to the OUTPUT
and electricity flows
between them.

Practice wiring circuits in
the red robot above. 
(Don't forget to come back!)

Go inside the robot and rewire
the bumpers to the thrusters
any way you like.

To start the robot moving,
put it against a wall.

This is the TOOLKIT.
Inside are tools and
parts you need to wire
circuits.

Press C to become the cursor
and pick up the Toolkit.

Carry it into the next room.

You can open and close the
Toolkit by pressing T.
Try it a few times. Then
take the Toolkit into the
next room.

Open the Toolkit and move on top
of the Remote Control or Solder-
pen. Then press SPACEBAR to
become that object. Practice
changing back and forth.
Leave the Toolkit here.

Take out some parts and watch
the COUNTER change. It tells how
many parts are left.
Press C to become the cursor.

NO
TOOLKITS
ALLOWED!

Do you want the Toolkit? Press
T to summon it. Drop the Tool-
kit. Then press T to open and 
close it.

You can make the cursor
HOT with electricity.
Press H.

Pass the hot cursor over
the antenna INPUT to turn
the antenna on.

Press H again to make the
cursor cold.

Then turn the Remote Control on
and change to the cursor.

You can take parts in and out
of the Toolkit with the cursor.

To take a part out, move on top
of it and press SPACEBAR. To put
it back, drop it anywhere in the
Toolkit.

~
 NODES

LOGIC
GATES -}

A full Toolkit has 10 flipflops
(10-FF), 15 nodes (15-N) and
35 gates (35-G).

MORE
CIRCUIT
IDEAS
{-

Be sure the Robot Odyssey I
disk is in the drive.

Then press ESC.









To go back to the room you
just left, press RETURN.

A node makes electricity
`branch" to two places.

Take a node from the Toolkit and
carry it to the next room.

Wire the INPUT
(circle) of the 
node to the 
OUTPUT of the 
CONTACT sensor.
Wire the node 
OUTPUTS to the
thrusters.

Drop the blue key so that it
touches the sensor. Electricity 
flows to both thrusters.

A flipflop is like
a light switch. It
`flips" electricity
from one output to
the other.

Take a flipflop from the
Toolkit. Put the hot cursor
on one INPUT at a time to
make the electricity
`flip" and `flop."

Go inside the robot and
wire the orange OUTPUT of
the flipflop to the thruster
on the right. Sit on the
eye to see what you did!
NOT-gate

(Turn the Remote 
Control on.)
XOR-gate -}
OR-gate

A NOT-gate inverts
electricity flow.
It turns on when its
INPUT is NOT on.

Take a NOT-gate from the
Toolkit and use the hot 
cursor to see how it
works.

Wire the NOT-gate OUTPUT
to the antenna INPUT.

The antenna beeps when
the crystal is NOT touching
the CONTACT sensor.

An AND-gate turns on
when its left AND
right INPUT are on.

Take an AND-gate from the
Toolkit and test it with 
the hot cursor.

Wire the AND-gate OUTPUT
to the antenna INPUT.

The antenna beeps when the
key is left AND up from 
this DIRECTIONAL sensor.

An EXCLUSIVE-OR-
gate (XOR-gate) 
turns on when one 
OR the other INPUT 
is on, NOT both.

Take an XOR-gate from the
Toolkit and test it with
the hot cursor.

Wire the XOR-gate OUTPUT
to the antenna INPUT.

The antenna beeps when
either the key or the
crystal is in the room,
but not both.

An OR-gate turns on
when one OR the other
INPUT is on, or both.

Take an OR-gate from the
Toolkit and use the hot
cursor to see how it
works.

Wire the OR-gate OUTPUT
to the antenna INPUT.

The antenna beeps when
the key is above OR
left of the sensor.

Try these robot circuits in the
robot below. See the manual for
solutions.

When you connect inputs to
outputs, you create CIRCUITS.

Change to the cursor and pick
up part of this circuit.

The wire will stretch as you
move, but will break if you
leave the room.
ROBOT

LEFT-WALL-CRAWLER
  Rewire the NOT-gate to the
  thruster on the right.

PING-PONG
  Unwire the NOT-gate. Use a
  second flipflop wired the
  same way as the robot in the
  flipflop example above.

KEY-PHOBE 
  Wire a key DIRECTIONAL sensor's 
  OUTPUTS to the thrusters they 
  point toward.

NON-KEY-GRABBER
  Wire a key CONTACT sensor to
  a NOT-gate. Wire the NOT-gate
  to the grabber INPUT.

CRYSTAL-SIGNALER
  Wire a crystal IN-SAME-ROOM
  sensor to the antenna.

C  Become the Cursor.
    SPACEBAR picks up/drops.

T  Summon Toolkit to your room.
   Open/close Toolkit in room.
Tip }
TOOLKIT

Here you will learn to use the:
     
    ^ Remote Control
    ^ Solderpen
    ^ Toolkit

If you don't know about ROBOT
ANATOMY, press ESC to go back
to the menu.

Press SPACEBAR to `freeze" the
electricity. The Remote Control
turns white.

Press R to become the
Remote Control.

When you have learned
all about the Toolkit,
go this way.

Now you know how to use the 
Solderpen, Remote Control, and
Toolkit.

You also know how nodes, flip-
flops, and logic gates work.

You can use these to design and 
build robots in ROBOTROPOLIS
or the INNOVATION LAB.

Press ESC when you are ready to
go back to the menu.
